    <item>
      <title>Utbrudd av influensa: – Ta vaksinen nå</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/utbrudd-av-influensa_-_-ta-vaksinen-na-1.18089136</link>
      <description>Vinterens influensautbrudd er i gang. Samtidig øker koronasmitten.
Det opplyser Folkehelseinstituttet torsdag.
– Beskyttelse mot influensa og covid-19 oppnås én til to uker etter at du har tatt vaksine. Det er derfor viktig at de som er anbefalt vaksine tar den nå, før smitten øker ytterligere, sier overlege Ingvild Fjeldheim ved FHI.
Vaksine er det viktigste tiltaket for å beskytte risikogrupper og eldre mot alvorlig influensa- og koronasykdom, heter det.
Men forsinkelser i leveransene har ført til at enkelte kommuner har måttet vente med vaksineringen. Dette problemet skal imidlertid være løst nå.
– Har du måtte utsette vaksineringen fordi vaksinen ikke var tilgjengelig, oppfordrer vi deg til å ta vaksine nå, sier Fjeldheim.
Disse anbefales å ta influensavaksinen:
• Alle fra fylte 65 år.
• Barn og voksne i definerte risikogrupper.
• Gravide etter 12. svangerskapsuke, og tidligere i svangerskapet ved tilleggsrisiko.
• Helsepersonell med nær pasientkontakt.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Nusa-dobbel for Leipzig i Meisterligaen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.

      <description>To menn er pågrepet etter en voldshendelse utenfor et utested i Arendal natt til søndag.

      <description>Timon Haugan leverte med presset som leder etter første omgang og kjørte inn til seier på slalåmen i Gurgl. Han ble med det første nordmann med verdenscupseier i Gurgl.
24 år gamle Eirik Hystad Solberg overrasket stort på og ble nummer to - hans første pallplass på toppnivå.
Atle Lie McGrath var nummer to før finaleomgangen, men hektet i en port og forsvant ut. I frustrasjon kastet han stavene og ble liggende ved siden av løypa. Også Henrik Kristoffersen, som var nummer seks etter første omgang, kjørte ut i finalen.
Lucas Pinheiro Braathen jaktet sin tredje strake seier - men 26-åringen kjørte ut i første omgang.</description>

      <title>Karoline Grøtting best av alle på sesongåpningens siste dag – skiskytter imponerte</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/karoline-grotting-best-av-alle-pa-sesongapningens-siste-dag-_-skiskytter-imponerte-1.18086614</link>
      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ Independent and employee owned - local news stories, weather, sports, events and more Thu, 26 Nov 2026 01:14:55 +0000 en-CA hourly 1 https://cheknews.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/cropped-CHEK-Mark-512x512-1-200x200.png?crop=1 CHEK https://cheknews.ca/ 32 32 70014466 Ministry of Social Development mandate letter shows changes coming to drug policies https://cheknews.ca/ministry-of-social-development-mandate-letter-shows-changes-coming-to-drug-policies-1364363/ Thu, 26 Nov 2026 01:14:53 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364363

The Ministry of Social Development's mandate letter calls for the end of safe supply and the review and reform of overdose prevention sites.

The post Ministry of Social Development mandate letter shows changes coming to drug policies appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The mandate letter for the Ministry of Social Development will lead to some big changes around drug policy.

The letter calls on the minister to end the safe drug supply and to direct that funding to
prevention, treatment and recovery.

It also mandates a review and reform of overdose prevention sites.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

Jan Mahoney, who’s advocated for drug users since losing her 21-year-old son Michael to an overdose in 2018, says she hopes the B.C. government doesn’t close OPS’s like other provinces have and she’s opposed to the government removing safe supply.

“It’s going to result in more deaths even though our safe supply program is very small. There were only, at maximum three thousand people enrolled,” said Maoney.

A public safety advocate in Nanaimo, though, supports the reform of overdose prevention sites.

“It’s a magnet for drug dealers to come by. They’ve got an audience that is right there, ready, willing and just very vulnerable to buying illegal drugs, so we need a better model,” said Kevan Shaw.

Shaw also supports the ending of safe supply noting the documented diversion of some of those drugs onto the streets.

“This all needs to be tightened up. We need to get these people off the drugs into a secure facility and if that means getting them into some form of mandatory care, then that’s what definitely needs to be done,” said Shaw.

Nanaimo’s mayor has seen many of the problems first hand.

“The OPS sites have been a very mixed challenge for every community,” said Leonard Krog.

Nanaimo’s City hall borders the OPS. In 2025 city staff recommended fencing city properties because of social disorder and petty crime.

“Many of us have said for years that the government had to look at the whole program, the whole issue of safe supply and secure involuntary care, the street disorder, the petty crime, all of the horrible mix that constitutes our street disorder. The end result is a not surprising change in government,” said Krog.

Krog says safer supply has a vital role in a full continuum of care but that full continuum of care was never in place.

He says the focus on recovery services is popular and necessary, one he hopes will be effective as no one wants to see so much misery on the street

Another notable change in the Social Development ministry’s mandate letter is to ensure an increase in disability assistance by $100 per month and establish an annual review of assistance rates.

It also calls on the minister to raise the annual persons with disabilities (PWD) earnings exemption to $30,000 “so people can earn substantially more before their assistance is reduced.”

]]> 1364363 Greater Victoria man hopes to bring joy to Ukrainian children through lacrosse https://cheknews.ca/greater-victoria-man-hopes-to-bring-joy-to-ukrainian-children-through-lacrosse-1364254/ Thu, 26 Nov 2026 00:39:43 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364254

A Greater Victoria lacrosse player is hoping to bring moments of joy and normalcy to Ukrainian children through sport.

The post Greater Victoria man hopes to bring joy to Ukrainian children through lacrosse appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Noah Beckett scores a goal for his lacrosse team at Lake Erie College.

Now back home in Greater Victoria, the former collegiate player is bringing that passion for the game to a new generation — with plans to introduce lacrosse to young people in Ukraine.

For Beckett, it’s about more than just the sport. It’s about sharing an opportunity to connect, learn and grow through the game.

Watch the video below:

Loading the player...

“If I can get one stick in one kid’s hands, and make him smile, for one day out of the dark grey years that they’ve had over there, that would be something just incredible to me,” Beckett said.

Beckett is working with Vancouver Island Supports Ukraine, a volunteer-led organization fundraising $100,000 to purchase equipment for a hospital and schools as Ukraine faces its fourth winter of war.

But his efforts go beyond providing essential supplies. Beckett also wants to give young Ukrainians the opportunity to experience the benefits of sport.

“The goal is to get around 100 sets of gear, which would include anything from cleats to chest pads, elbows, gloves, helmets and of course, a stick to be able to get these kids to play together,” Beckett said.

The goal is to collect enough donated equipment to allow students from different schools to compete against one another.

But more importantly, Beckett hopes the opportunity to play will give young people a chance to step away from the realities of war, even if only for a little while.

Chris Balmer is a volunteer with VISU and a retired Camosun College counsellor who launched the Student Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy in January 2016, making Camosun the first college in British Columbia to create such a strategy.

“Sport, in many ways, is sort of an extension of learning how to behave in society. But it’s fun. I think that’s where the unique piece of this comes in. There’s not an opportunity for the kids to experience joy. For them to exercise and get rid of pent-up trauma in their bodies,” Balmer said.

For young Ukrainians, the chance to play sports comes against the backdrop of a war that’s defined their lives. For 21-year-old philosophy student, Uliana Kolesnyk, years of war have taken their toll.

“It’s just living with the constant feeling of fear and hope at the same time. You always hope for things to get better. Because there is no other way you can win this war. You just have to keep your hopes up,” Kolesnyk said in Lutsk, Ukraine, in November 2025.

And it’s that longing for normalcy Balmer says a sport, like lacrosse, can provide.

“Sport provides a sense of an organized and predictable environment. Where they can actually have rules and regulations. And they can actually connect and bond with each other, and attach, and have normal relationships. And build trust and have cooperative behaviour,” Balmer said.

Donations can be dropped off at Langford Fire Hall One off Veteran’s Memorial Parkway,
or contact Vancouver Island Supports Ukraine.

]]> 1364254 ‘I want these rooms open’: B.C. premier promises to reverse rural ER closures https://cheknews.ca/i-want-these-rooms-open-b-c-premier-promises-to-reverse-rural-er-closures-1364255/ Wed, 25 Nov 2026 23:45:42 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364255

]]>

Six days after a 48-year-old Port Hardy mother died after being locked out of her community’s emergency room, B.C.’s new premier, Lorne Doerkson, is promising to “fix” things.

“I want to send my love and prayers to the family. I am so disappointed our healthcare system has arrived to where it is after all of these years. We intend to fix that. We are committed to keeping these hospitals open,” said Doerkson on Wednesday.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

After being sick for days, Courtney McCowan reportedly arrived 11 minutes after Port Hardy’s emergency room had closed for the night on Thursday, Nov. 19.

In medical distress, instead of being rushed inside to be seen by doctors, it was paramedics who were called to try and resuscitate her in the hospital parking lot.

“Why was she left on the concrete for 39 minutes outside a hospital dedicated to saving people’s lives?” McCowan’s brother, Frank McCowan, asked CHEK News on Sunday.

“We can’t help but think it would have been avoided, you know, if she would have been able to get in and see a doctor.”

As questions swirl around the circumstances of her death, why McCowan wasn’t brought indoors or seen by doctors just steps away, advocates believe the emergency room’s locked doors didn’t help.

“This started out as we’re going to close it temporarily at 5p.m., it’s been four years,” said Fran Jenkins, a Port Hardy resident who has been advocating for better healthcare in the community for years now.

“It’s not the first death. People are dying in transport to Port McNeil…How many lives does it take for you to go, ‘That’s enough, we better do something?'”

Time for managers to put their scrubs back on?

Port Hardy family physician Dr. Alex Nataros says the issue isn’t a lack of front-line healthcare workers but a badly set up system, and a lack of want and will from managers to deliver patient care.

“It is not a question of frontline providers, it is a question of organization and use of resources,” said Nataros. “We have more managers in Port Hardy hospital then we have frontline emerg. workers in Port Hardy emerg. hospital.”

Island Health has previously said it’s reviewing the circumstances of the case with BC Emergency Health Services. It’s unclear if that review will be made public.

Doerkson instructs Health Minister to keep ER rooms open

Today from Victoria, Doerkson handed his new Minister of Health, Ryan Peterson, his new mandate.

In it he details his expectations of a forthcoming clear plan, timeline and results, in part on rural healthcare.

“Keep rural emergency rooms and maternity wards open, backed by flexible staffing and a $50 million Rural Health Emergency Fund,” reads the minister’s mandate.

Doerkson also directed Peterson to launch a review to identify reforms that other universal public health systems have made that cut waits, expand capacity, keep ERs open and strengthen rural services.

“I’ve had a conversation with the Minister of Health. He is very clear that I want these rooms open,” said Doerkson. “We can put men and women on the moon. I am not convinced that we cannot keep these facilities open.”

With no clear timeline for the changes, overnight ER closures will likely continue in Port Hardy for now.

B.C. Premier Lorne Doerkson moved quickly after his first cabinet meeting Wednesday to order government workers back to the office and scrap the controversial SOGI program in schools.

Doerkson made the directives alongside an announcement that the government will tender a design for a 10-lane Massey bridge to replace the NDP’s tunnel project, with the goal of reaching a final decision on whether to build the bridge before Christmas.

Watch the video below:

Loading the player...

On SOGI, the sexual orientation and gender identity learning module in schools, the new Conservative government pulled the material off websites immediately and Dokerson said it will be replaced by other anti-bullying and safety material. 

“We do want to provide safe spaces for our kids to learn, they should absolutely be able to attend there, but SOGI has become a frustration for so many, and I believe that we have to remove it,” he said.

Doerkson also spoke about new mandate letters to his 18-person cabinet, and six ministers of state, which give them marching orders and priorities for the beginning of his government. The letters outline sharp policy pivots for the Conservative government in health care, education, environment, transportation, taxes and resource development.

RELATED: Lorne Doerkson unveils new mandate letters for B.C. cabinet

“We’re very committed to a different direction, and I think we’ve shown that all throughout the campaign, and I think it’s clear that British Columbians have given us a mandate to do exactly that,” Doerkson told reporters.

The premier has asked Environment Minister Á’a:líya Warbus to end the NDP’s CleanBC climate program, scrap EV sales mandates and restore public access to all Crown land and parks. He said he’s still committed to trying to fit into national and international climate change plans where appropriate.

Health Minister Ryan Peterson was tasked with keeping rural ERs open, in the wake of a Port Hardy mother who died in medical distress outside a closed ER.

“I am so disappointed that our healthcare system has arrived where it is after all of these years, and we intend to fix that,” he said. “We are committed to keeping these hospitals open.”

Peterson is also directed to use public money to fund medical procedures at private clinics in Canada and the United States if wait times in B.C. are at unacceptable levels, as well as conduct a 100-day review of the health system and recruit more doctors and nurses.

Education Minister Lynne Block was directed to restore letter grades in Grades 4-9, restore the singing of O Canada every morning and base future $10-a-day childcare spaces on need.

Other mandate letters focused on the expansion of natural gas, mining and resource projects and legislated permitting times. 

Doerkson directed Indigenous Relations Minister Scott McInnis to not only repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) but also craft a new law to defend private property, as well as make public all the information on government negotiations with First Nations involving land claims.

On housing, Doerkson directed minister Cathie Ounsted to return control of housing policies to local municipalities —  though he stopped short of ordering the repeal of short-term rental restrictions and vacancy taxes, saying he needs to review them first.

Transportation Minister Trevor Halford was ordered to conduct an independent review of BC Ferries, to look at overhead and executive costs inside the corporation, as well as get working wireless internet on ships.

The Opposition NDP said the mandate letters are worrisome, especially in healthcare which could lead to a two-tier system if some patients are being sent to private clinics.

“The letters reflect a real lack of clarity about what their plans is for programs for British Columbians,” said interim NDP leader Jennifer Whiteside.

“I don’t see a reflection of the primary concerns for people that I hear: healthcare, housing, affordability.”

BC Green leader Emily Lowan called the mandate letters concerning. “These are floundering culture war signals instead of the desperate, immediate relief British Columbians need.

]]> 1364274 Health Canada warns of rare vision loss risk with Ozempic and other semaglutide drugs https://cheknews.ca/health-canada-warns-of-rare-vision-loss-risk-with-ozempic-and-other-semaglutide-drugs-1364256/ Wed, 25 Nov 2026 23:05:30 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364256

Health Canada has issued a warning about a "very rare" risk of vision loss with Ozempic, Wegovy and other semaglutide drugs.

The post Health Canada warns of rare vision loss risk with Ozempic and other semaglutide drugs appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Health Canada has issued a warning about a “very rare” risk of vision loss with Ozempic, Wegovy and other semaglutide drugs. 

In the warning issued Wednesday, the department saidit has completed a safety review “that found a possible link between prescription semaglutide drugs and the risk of non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.” 

The eye condition, also known as NAION, “causes sudden painless vision loss or vision changes due to reduced blood flow to the optic nerve.”

Health Canada said it is working with semaglutide manufacturers to include warnings about the condition in their product monographs. 

Patients taking the diabetes and weight loss drugs should talk to their health-care provider about the potential risks before taking them, the warning said. 

Anyone currently taking semaglutide should get urgent medical attention if they experience blurring, cloudiness, rapidly worsening sight or sudden vision loss.  

Health Canada said its safety review focused on semaglutide drugs, but it is also assessing the risk with all other GLP-1 drugs.  

Earlier in November, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced manufacturers of all GLP-1 medications  — including tirzepatide drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound — must add a warning about NAION to their product labels. 

Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy is the most common type of damage to the optic nerve in adults over 50, Health Canada’s summary of its review said. 

People with diabetes, high blood pressure and high cholesterol are at increased risk for the condition. 

The link between semaglutide and NAION “is not fully understood,” the summary said, but a rapid drop in blood sugar levels after using the medication “may cause swelling of the optic nerve and reduce its blood supply, especially in individuals with other risk factors.”

It’s not known how long it takes symptoms of the condition to develop, the summary said.  

In an email on Wednesday, the Canadian Association of Optometrists said it has been aware of the rare risk of NAION “for some time.”

“If you’re starting a GLP-1 medication and haven’t had an eye exam in the last year, it’s a good idea to get your eyes checked. It’s also important to let your optometrist know that you’re taking the medication,” said Dr. Allison Scott, the association’s president. 

“Anyone experiencing sudden vision loss should seek immediate eye care. An optometrist can assess the issue and, where necessary, facilitate an urgent referral to an ophthalmologist,” she said. 

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 25, 2026.

The post B.C. removing SOGI materials from government sites, will remove from schools appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

SOGI 123 materials are being removed from B.C. government websites effective immediately, and work will begin to remove them from schools, the province announced Wednesday.

SOGI 123 is an inclusive education initiative designed to make schools safer and more inclusive for all students that was brought in by the then-B.C. Liberal government in 2016/2017.

Now, the Conservative government, run by a premier who was part of the party that introduced the program, is rescinding it.

“Parents are responsible for their children and they should have a say in what those children are taught,” Premier Lorne Doerkson said in a news release.

“SOGI has become a lightning rod of division in this province and it has pulled attention away from what our schools are there to do. We are acting now to reset that conversation and to bring parents back into it.”

The news release says the government has removed all SOGI 123 material from government websites and materials, including those provided to schools. Now, the Ministry of Education and Child Care will work with school districts to remove it from schools.

“Every student in B.C. should be able to go to school and feel safe, and we will strengthen measures to protect all students,” Lynne Block, minister of education and child care, said in a news release.

“At the same time, parents have told us they want schools concentrating on the basics. Strong numeracy, literacy and critical thinking skills are what students need to succeed, and that is where our focus will be.”

The BC Teachers’ Federation says it is disappointed by the decision.

“First, let me be clear: BC teachers will always stand up for schools where all students and families feel welcome and see themselves represented. That will never change,” Carole Gordon, president of the BCTF, said in a news release.

“We’re disappointed by this decision, which appears to be rooted in misinformation about SOGI resources.”

Gordon says she is also uncertain about what exactly the announcement means.

“We also have questions about what this means in practice. Which resources does the government intend to remove? Those labelled SOGI 123? Books that reflect the diversity of our families? How far backward is this government trying to take us?” she asked.

“Amid that uncertainty, I want to offer some reassurance to our 2SLGBTQIA+ students, parents, colleagues, and families: Your rights have not changed. The BC Human Rights Code continues to protect against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity.”

She says B.C. teachers will continue building welcoming classrooms, nurturing a sense of belonging, and standing up for one another.

“Every child deserves to walk through the doors of their school feeling comfortable in who they are, knowing they have friends and adults in their corner,” Gordon said. “We’ll always stand up for that.”

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, whose huge pop hits included “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and were inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor’s death was confirmed by his family and band mates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran’s website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one’s own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award-winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the UK and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Visionary Award recipients.

The band’s 1981 debut album “Duran Duran” had their first hit single, “Planet Earth,” but it was “Rio” that transformed them into trans-Atlantic stars. The Rock Hall explained their appeal this way: “They were new wave outsiders who became music video stars — “Tiger Beat” fashion pinups who rocked arenas.”

How music videos made Duran Duran massively famous

The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as “Girls on Film” and “Union of the Snake” and the moody ballads “The Chauffeur” and “Save a Prayer.” Other hits in the coming years included “The Wild Boys,” “New Moon on Monday” and “Come Undone.” Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song “A View to a Kill” and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesizers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people’s walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labeled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan and that meant a lot to the band.

“It worked well for us,” drummer Roger Taylor told Rolling Stone. “It was genuine. I don’t think it was some sort of PR stunt. It was massive for us because she was the No. 1 icon of the early ’80s.”

The band’s success was in large part due to their videos, including their Antigua-set song “Rio,” which featured shots of the band in pastel suits sailing confidently on a yacht. For the album “Rio,” they shot three music videos in Sri Lanka — including “Save a Prayer,” which had John Taylor getting sprayed by an elephant — and two in Antigua, feeding MTV’s need to have a stream of visuals, something classic rock didn’t have.

“A lot of the success of the album is down to the power of the videos and the way it made the band omnipresent around the globe,” Le Bon told The Daily Beast in 2012. Andy Taylor agreed: “I don’t think we could have done it without MTV.”

John Taylor and keyboardist Nick Rhodes started the band as teenagers in the northern city of Birmingham in 1978, with a name inspired by a character in the Jane Fonda-starring sci-fi movie “Barbarella.” Roger Taylor, Le Bon and Andy Taylor joined soon after, with the British press referring to them as the “Fab Five.” Andy Taylor answered an ad in Melody Maker music magazine for a “Live-Wire Guitarist.” (None of the Taylors were related.)

“We all grew up on the same vinyl records and live gigs, from David Bowie to Roxy Music, The Sex Pistols and, of course, Chic. I could go to all those places as a player and developed a hybrid guitar style that fitted this amazing concept of a band,” Andy Taylor wrote in a letter read by the band during their Rock Hall induction.

Behind massive success, Taylor and band mates were distant

Duran Duran had the unenviable job of following Led Zeppelin at Live Aid in Philadelphia and performed “A View to a Kill,” “The Union of the Snake,” “Save a Prayer” and “The Reflex.” In his book, “Wild Child,” Andy Taylor revealed the band was, as he put it, “falling apart at the seams.”

“Everything should have been perfect, but privately we were screwed and in turmoil. When we came offstage in Philadelphia there were no congratulatory hugs or friendly smiles. It was like we were completely foreign to each other, and it would be the last time we played together for almost two decades.”

The various members all had some success with side projects: Le Bon, Rhodes and Roger Taylor recorded an album as Arcadia in 1985; John Taylor and Andy Taylor formed Power Station, a supergroup that included Robert Palmer, in 1984, having hits with “Some Like It Hot” and “Get It On.”

In 1986, the band came together to record the hit album produced with Nile Rodgers “Notorious” — with hits including the title single and “Skin Trade” — but Andy Taylor made his second exit from the group after some early recording sessions for the album. He would stay away for such albums as 1997’s “Medazzaland” and 2000′s “Pop Trash” — but returned for 2004’s “Astronaut.”

By 2007, Andy Taylor opted not to participate in the Timbaland-led “Red Carpet Massacre,” an attempt to harness a more youthful rhythmic vibe. “With Andy not turning up, it couldn’t be a rock record, so that whole album was an attempt to patch over the cracks with Andy missing,” John Taylor told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution in 2011.

Andy Taylor told The Scotsman in 2008: “People have wrongly assumed that I didn’t want to be in the band, but the opposite is true. I always wanted to be in a band, but Duran Duran had ceased to function as a band.”

At Duran Duran’s height, they were as famously destructive as any rock band. Andy Taylor in his memoir revealed he had a six-year cocaine habit and band members trashed hotel rooms, argued with management about money and had high-end shopping sprees.

Andy Taylor was the first of the Duran boys to get married, tying the knot with Tracey in 1982 and having four children, Andy, Georgie, Bethy and Izzy, and a grandson, Albie. He is survived by all of them, and they credited his devotion to them in a family statement.

“For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home,” the family statement said.

In 2023, he released the album “Man’s a Wolf to Man,” his first solo release in over 30 years. On the title track, he sang: “Last night/I dreamt someone loved me/And life was not surreal/Someone’s souvenir.”

A voice actor based out of Nanaimo who plays a radio announcer in blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto VI says he’s been thrilled by the response he’s received for his role in the game.

Matt Fogarty is billed as the radio imaging voice for Flash FM, one of the game’s roughly two dozen fictional radio stations. Flash FM is the game’s pop station, featuring songs from real artists like Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Justice and more.

“The response has been overwhelming. Overwhelmingly positive,” said Fogarty in an interview with CHEK News on Wednesday.

“I’ve heard from friends that I haven’t talked to since high school, I’ve heard from a lot of my radio friends and colleagues, of course, a lot of media response, which is great,” he said.

Fogarty only learned he was featured in Grand Theft Auto VI once the game came out on Nov. 19. The game, which is rumoured to cost more than $1 billion to make, made nearly $4 billion over its opening weekend.

When he took the role, the title of the project was secret.

“I’m a fan of the game, so I knew there was a new Grand Theft Auto game coming out, so I was hopeful, but there was no level of certainty there,” he said. “It wasn’t official until release day and I saw my name in the credits on the Rockstar Games website.”

“It was cool. I started getting some messages like, ‘Hey, is that your voice in the game?’ and I was like, OK, I’m starting to put things together, and sure enough I went to check the official credits and there I was.”

RELATED: After a 13-year wait, ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ arrives with enormous hype and expectations

Fogarty has a long background in radio, including 14 years in Nanaimo, and has been a full time voice actor for more than half a decade.

He says he’s impressed by the breadth of the radio system in the game.

“It was really cool. This was a custom-created station for the game,” said Fogarty. “Radio is a big part of the game, you can access the in-game radio stations in your car, there’s radios scattered throughout the game that you can turn on and tune into your favourite station.” 

“So a lot of the work that I do is radio imaging. So the same kind of work, in terms of workflow, it was very similar to my normal day voicing copy for radio stations across Canada and the U.S.,” he said.

While the game has been in development for years – its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013 – Fogarty said he didn’t record his lines until this summer. He voiced his part all in one session.

“I’ve been doing voice acting full time now for six or seven years, but I don’t think I’d ever realized I’d be associated with a franchise this big,” he said.
